The UE may be configured to measure and report, subject to UE capability, via [higher layer parameter] the DL RSTD, DL PRS-RSRP, DL PRS-RSRPP, or UE Rx-Tx time difference using receiver frequency hopping for a DL PRS resource, with bandwidth that may be greater than the maximum UE bandwidth, within a configured measurement gap. The UE performing receiver frequency hopping may be configured to report via [higher layer parameter] one measurement associated with one received frequency hop or one measurement based on multiple hops of the DL PRS. In RRC_CONNECTED mode, the UE is expected to use a single instance of a configured measurement gap to receive all hops of the DL PRS using receiver frequency hopping. < Unchanged parts are omitted > --------------------------------------- End of Text Proposal ---------------------------------- | ---------------------------- Start of Text Proposal for TS 38.214 ----------------------------- < Unchanged parts are omitted > 5.1.6.5 PRS reception procedure < Unchanged parts are omitted > For a UE configured with DL PRS Processing Window(s), when the UE receives an activation/deactivation command, as described in clause 6.1.3.42 of [10, TS 38.321], for a DL PRS processing window activation, and when the UE would transmit a PUCCH with HARQ-ACK information in slot n corresponding to the PDSCH carrying the command, the corresponding actions in [10, TS 38.321] and the UE assumptions shall be applied starting from the first slot that is after slot where  is the SCS configuration for the PUCCH. The UE is not expected to be indicated with more than 4 activated DL PRS processing windows across all active DL BWPs and is not expected to be indicated with the activated DL PRS processing windows that overlap in time. {"chunk_id":"R1-2503344-001","collection":"ran1_tdoc_chunks","metadata":{"source":["vivo"],"tdocNumber":"R1-2503344","title":"Draft reply LS on differentiation of sDCI mTRP, mDCI mTRP and sTRP"},"point_id":"3093033622428271755"}
2500013 (R2-2411244)], RAN1 has reached the further agreement regarding question 2a and 2b: Regarding the issue on differentiation of sTRP and sDCI mTRP, we provide our views in this contribution. 2 Discussion As discussed in our previous contributions [R1-2501830], for simultaneous unified TCI state(s) update for a list of cells, what to be differentiated are: sTRP in Rel-17 UTCI framework and sDCI mTRP in Rel-18 eUTCI framework. Among two alternatives, we prefer Alt2 due to following reasons: The essential difference between sTRP and sDCI based mTRP is the number of indicated TCI states, which is determined by which kind of TCI state MAC CE command, among Unified TCI States Activation/Deactivation MAC CE (TS 38.321 clause 6.1.3.47), Enhanced Unified TCI States Activation/Deactivation MAC CE for Joint TCI States (TS 38.321 clause 6.1.3.70), or Enhanced Unified TCI States Activation/Deactivation MAC CE for Separate TCI States (TS 38.321 clause 6.1.3.71), is received. When a UE receives any above TCI state activation MAC CE command, the TCI states are activated for all CCs/DL BWPs in simultaneousU-TCI-UpdateListX if configured, which guarantees all CCs in the list will be indicated with same number of TCI states. Given the following conclusion drawn in RAN1#115, UE does not expect to receive Unified TCI States Activation/Deactivation MAC CE after receiving Enhanced Unified TCI States Activation/Deactivation MAC CE for Joint TCI States, or Enhanced Unified TCI States Activation/Deactivation MAC CE for Separate TCI States. In other words, once a UE operates as sDCI mTRP in a set of CCs/BWPs, it will never operate as sTRP anymore. Therefore, there is no need to differentiate the cells operated as sTRP or sDCI mTRP by any RRC parameters as given in Alt1 because the current spec has guaranteed all CCs in the list operate in the same mode. However, current field description is incomplete without capturing the two MAC CEs for s-DCI based mTRP introduced in Rel-18. We propose to update the field description as follows: 3 Recommended reply to the LS With the above understanding, kindly please find the replies on the second issue below: 2. sTRP vs sDCI mTRP Question 2a: RAN2 would like to ask if RAN1 has any concern on the above highlight sentence? Answer 2a: Yes. There is no need to differentiate the cells operated as sTRP or sDCI mTRP by any RRC parameters because the current spec has guaranteed all CCs in the list should operate in the same mode. The essential difference between sTRP and sDCI based mTRP is the number of indicated TCI states, which is determined by which kind of TCI state MAC CE command, among Unified TCI States Activation/Deactivation MAC CE (TS 38.321 clause 6.1.3.47), Enhanced Unified TCI States Activation/Deactivation MAC CE for Joint TCI States (TS 38.321 clause 6.1.3.70), or Enhanced Unified TCI States Activation/Deactivation MAC CE for Separate TCI States (TS 38.321 clause 6.1.3.71), is received. When a UE receives any above TCI state activation MAC CE command, the TCI states are activated for all CCs/DL BWPs in simultaneousU-TCI-UpdateListX if configured, which guarantees all CCs in the list will be indicated with same number of TCI states. The sentence highlighted in yellow is not proper to differentiate sDCI based mTRP and sTRP. Moreover, the field description does not capture TCI state activation/deactivation by the Enhanced Unified TCI States Activation/Deactivation MAC CE for Joint TCI States as specified in TS 38.321 clause 6.1.3.70, or Enhanced Unified TCI States Activation/Deactivation MAC CE for Separate TCI States as specified in TS 38.321 clause 6.1.3.71 for sDCI mTRP in Rel-18 eUTCI.
